**Finding: T4C — compliant (preferred level).**

Section 9.4 hits every preferred element of the rule:

- **Customer convenience right over Agreement or Order Form** — "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part".
- **Notice ≤ 30 days** — "upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor".
- **Pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, no penalty** — "Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date", with Customer owing Fees only for conforming Services through the effective date.
- **No Vendor convenience right in a committed term** — "Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term."

I checked the rest of the termination architecture: §§ 9.1–9.3 are cause-based (breach, insolvency, security/legal/IP failures), § 9.5 preserves cumulative remedies, § 24.4 blocks Vendor termination on Customer change of control, and § 8.2 auto-renewal gives the non-renewal right to Customer only — so Vendor has no convenience or notice-based exit anywhere in the document.

One note, not a redline: § 2.1's take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" sits in tension with § 9.4's no-penalty exit. That is the minimum-commitment bargain and belongs under MINCOMMIT; flagging it here would double-count the same commercial term. No redline proposed.
